## Summary

- pin one `origin/main` base snapshot for each repair Codex edit pass
- stop edit workers from refetching, rebasing, and revalidating solely because `main` advances after validation

target.title: fix(dashboard): link apply health cards to source runs
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep every apply-health dashboard alert linked to the workflow run that generated that health snapshot.
- Preserve the mutable top-level status link only as a fallback for older snapshots.
- Prevent later review/status writes from replacing a retained apply-health source link.

## Problem

The dashboard retained an apply-health warning while later review/status writes replaced the top-level `run_url`. The "Pruning sweep blocked" card therefore opened a later, unrelated review run. In the captured production case it linked to [run 29091926566](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091926566), a successful hot-review run whose apply job was skipped.

![Before fix: dashboard alert pointing at an unrelated workflow run](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/codex/fix-apply-health-link/docs/proof/dashboard-apply-health-run-link/mislinked-apply-health-alert.png)

## After-fix behavior proof

The redacted local dashboard below is generated by `dashboard/worker.ts` from the captured production status shape: the apply warning originated in [run 29091427650](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091427650), while a later status write pointed at [run 29091585991](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091585991). No live state, workflow, or deployment was changed to create this proof.

![After fix: generated dashboard card](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/codex/fix-apply-health-link/docs/proof/dashboard-apply-health-run-link/after-fix-local-dashboard.png)

Browser verification from that generated card:

```text
element: link "open run"
href: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091427650
click result: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091427650
later root status URL: https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091585991
```

This demonstrates both the rendered link target and successful navigation to the originating apply run, rather than the later status run.

## Implementation

- Stamp `run_url` into a fresh apply-health snapshot.
- Read the nested immutable health URL before the mutable root status URL.
- Retain an existing health object unchanged during non-apply status updates; only a fresh health payload gets the current run URL.
- Add reader precedence and writer-preservation coverage in focused dashboard and sweep-status test files.

## Validation

- `pnpm run build:all`
- `node --test test/sweep-status.test.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts` (64 passing)
- `pnpm run lint:src`
- `pnpm run lint:dashboard`
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/clawsweeper.ts test/clawsweeper.test.ts test/sweep-status.test.ts dashboard/worker.ts test/dashboard-worker.test.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Review closeout

- `codex review --uncommitted`: clean; no actionable findings.
- `codex review --base origin/main`: clean; no actionable findings.

The branch review also attempted the broad unit suite. Its workflow-helper cases are blocked on this Windows host because `bash` resolves through WSL, whose default `docker-desktop` distribution has no `/bin/bash`; the focused changed-surface proof above passed.

## Risks and rollout

New snapshots gain a nested source URL. Existing snapshots continue using the top-level URL fallback, so the change is backward compatible. It affects dashboard observability only; sweep, comment, label, and close behavior are unchanged.

## Links

- State snapshot with the original apply run: [0557127d580c](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper-state/commit/0557127d580c2e4a7ac6f59ea84e3c592135461e)
- Production symptom: [run 29091926566](https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/29091926566)

target.title: test: support CRLF workflow assertions
target.body:
## Summary

Make the failed-review retry workflow-content test portable across LF and CRLF checkouts.

## Problem

PR #445 added assertions that read `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` and required LF-only newlines. With `core.autocrlf=true` on Windows, Git checks out that unchanged workflow with CRLF line endings, so `sweep workflow forwards source revision and bounds drift requeue` failed even though the job exists and is correctly configured.

## Implementation

- Allow either `LF` or `CRLF` in the two newline-sensitive workflow assertions.
- Preserve the asserted job names and permission structure.
- Format the long updated assertion with the repository formatter.
- Do not modify `.github/workflows/sweep.yml` or runtime code.

## Validation

- `node --test test/failed-review-retry.test.ts` — passed: 16/16 on a checkout with `core.autocrlf=true`; `sweep.yml` contained 3,287 CRLF lines.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check test/failed-review-retry.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm run build` — passed.
- `pnpm run lint:scripts` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm run test:unit` — 765 passed, 11 failed, 1 skipped. The 11 failures are pre-existing Windows-host noise from the unavailable WSL `/bin/bash` (plus dependent local-range fixtures). The same failures reproduce from the clean `origin/main` checkout; on that checkout the original LF-only failed-review assertion also fails.

## Proof

Before this change, the focused test reproduced as 15 passed and 1 failed, with the failure at the LF-only `requeue-source-revision-drift` assertion. After this change, the same CRLF checkout passes all 16 tests. The production requeue workflow was already present and correct; this PR changes test portability only.

The CI follow-up was formatting-only: CI ran 1,449 tests with 0 failures, then reported this test file as needing formatting. Commit `b487cccd6df23b42fc58d6bd78a86e37ae823e04` applies the formatter's line wrap without changing the regex or behavior.

## Codex review closeout

- Initial command: `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no accepted or rejected findings.
- Follow-up dirty command: `codex review --uncommitted` — clean; no accepted or rejected findings.
- Follow-up branch command: `codex review --base origin/main` — clean; no accepted or rejected findings.
- Proof rerun: focused test passed 16/16 after the formatting commit.
- Final result: clean.

## Risks and rollout

Low risk: test-only regex widening from `\n` to `\r?\n`, followed by formatting-only wrapping. It still requires the same adjacent workflow structure and does not change production behavior. No release note is needed.

## Links

- Regression introduced by #445.

target.title: fix: guard low-signal PR closes
target.body:
## Summary

- require a live `mergeable=false` / `mergeable_state=dirty` conflict before applying `low_signal_unmergeable_pr`
- require dated current-head evidence and at least the configured stale interval without contributor comments, reviews, inline comments, or head activity
- fail closed during stale F-rated promotion and route trusted low-signal close markers through the authoritative apply path
- leave duplicate, superseded, and implemented-on-main close reasons unchanged

## Why

OpenClaw PRs #91271 and #91280 were closed as low-signal even though both were `MERGEABLE` / `UNSTABLE` and their contributor had commented and force-pushed roughly 4.5 hours earlier. The old final guard checked maintainer signals but did not verify the claimed conflict or contributor activity.

## Validation

- `pnpm test` — 1454 passed
- `pnpm run build:all`
- `pnpm run lint`
- `pnpm run format:check`
- focused promotion/router suite — 134 passed
- GPT-5.6 Sol High structured review — clean
